data.takes: A DRAFT, not signed, from EXPLORATION-0001 on this same record. Warns: three passes are flagged reach_q 2, one of them (2024-10-30) with a height 1.776 m off, and one unflagged pass (2024-03-26, dark_frac 0.692) with a height 0.939 m off. Used as a draft: I do not look for the bad passes again. I apply the flag screen from the start, name those two dates, and check in one look whether the same passes have odd widths, since the request expects the same passes to fool both.
A DRAFT, not signed, and it says it contradicts a signed recipe. Takes: give scores with and without the flag screen. Not relied on beyond that.

Signed. Width carries its own uncertainty field and quality attributes are gates. The reach product reports width as observed. The fixture holds width_m and no width uncertainty, so that cannot be used here.

Signed. Rules in the pairing: nearest reading within a stated tolerance, 15 minutes at this gauge. The scores it defines are for height; for width there is no datum question, but width and stage are different quantities, so only whether they move together can be asked.
Signed. Say the level: reach level width, one reach.

data.about: SWOT RiverSP reach width as a check on reach height at a leveed reach
data.text: Seen while exploring calendar 2024 at reach 74210000331 against USGS-07374000, Version D. Width does rise with stage (rank correlation +0.744 on the 47 unflagged pairs; +0.740 on all 50), by about 8.03 m of width per metre of stage over a 1.64 to 10.33 m range, but the spread of width about that line is 25.4 m, which is the width change of roughly three metres of stage. And the two passes whose heights were far off (2024-10-30 and 2024-03-26, named in a draft page from EXPLORATION-0001, not signed) have unremarkable widths: ranks 12 and 8 of 50 from the narrowest, while the widths furthest from the median are on other dates with ordinary flags. So at this reach width neither tracks stage finely enough to check a height nor singles out the passes with bad heights. What would reopen it: a reach whose banks slope, where width changes by much more per metre of stage than its pass-to-pass scatter.

data.summary: Width follows stage only coarsely at this leveed reach and does not flag the passes with bad heights: a dead end here, recorded with what would reopen it
